label: rare copy-phase blip in length-9 sequences (input f/o around recall step 2)
explanation: Very sparse and weak (0.03% of steps, max activation 0.012). Fires only in the copy phase, almost only for L=9 (96% of mass; never for L<=7, never in original or delimiter phases, never on the first occurrence of a token). Within that it is concentrated at recall_idx 2 (t=11, ~47% of mass) and the last two copy steps (~31%), and on inputs f, o, z, j (~80% of mass). But each of these is a weak enrichment: L=9 copy has 0.3% precision, and the tightest simple conjunction (L=9, recall_idx 2, input f or o) reaches only 11% precision / 30% recall (dev F1 0.16). The strongest activations look like input f/o followed by output i/j, but that bigram predicate has low recall (7%). No coherent predicate found; it behaves like a near-threshold tail of a distributed code.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, o, z, j, 3, m; least: k, l, b, h) and the first original token (most: 1, p, q, h, m, a; least: c, i, 3, d); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, L=9 & t=11, t=16.
